overview: Evergrande Property Services Group is one of China's largest property management companies, managing approximately 601 million sq.m. of gross floor area as of end-2025 across residential, commercial and public-service properties. It was spun off and listed on HKEX in December 2020 as the property-services arm of China Evergrande Group, which was wound up and delisted from HKEX in August 2025; the company is now majority-owned (51.016%) by entities under the control of Evergrande's court-appointed liquidators, who are in exclusive talks to sell that stake to PAG. Operations and reporting are entirely PRC/Guangzhou-based and denominated in RMB despite the Cayman-incorporated, HKEX-listed holding structure.

business_model.summary: Revenue is overwhelmingly fee-for-service property management (84% of FY2025 revenue) supplemented by three smaller value-added segments. Property management fees are largely recurring (annual contracts tied to GFA under management), while community living, asset management and community operation services are more transactional/project-based, layered on top of the managed-property customer base.

revenue_streams.name: Community living services (group-buying, to-home, tourism, utilities)

business_model.customer_type: Mix of B2C (individual property owners paying management fees) and B2B/B2G (developers, commercial landlords, government/public-service clients such as hospitals, schools, rail transit and highway service areas)
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% PRC operations, reported in RMB; headquartered in Guangzhou, Guangdong. Essentially no non-China exposure despite the Cayman Islands/Hong Kong corporate wrapper.

competitive_position.market_position: Ranked No. 4 in the '2025 Top 100 Property Management Companies in China' per industry think-tank rankings, with scale (601m sq.m. GFA, ~100,500 employees) among the largest in the sector, but reputation and new-business momentum have been badly damaged by the parent's collapse.

moat_factors.description: Large existing portfolio of managed properties generates sticky, contracted recurring revenue even as new signings from related parties have stalled.

99.8% of FY2025 revenue now comes from third parties (vs. related parties), with third-party new signings reaching 45 million sq.m. in 2025 at a 92.1% entry/conversion rate, showing the business can win work independent of the former parent.

The Evergrande brand name is a significant liability post-scandal; new business wins likely occur despite, not because of, the brand, and management has had to rebuild trust with owners and institutional clients.
Property management contracts have some renewal inertia, but owners/developers can and do switch managers, especially where service quality or financial stability is in doubt.

Growing specialization in non-residential formats (hospitals, schools, rail transit, highway service areas, industrial parks) which carry higher saturated revenue per contract (~80% of new annual saturated revenue in 2025) and are less tied to Evergrande residential developments.

weaknesses: Legacy dependence on a since-liquidated parent for a meaningful share of historical GFA and brand association
Impaired receivables and collection difficulty from both related parties and owners who lost confidence amid the Evergrande scandal
Pending change-of-control overhang (PAG/liquidator stake sale) creates strategic uncertainty for management, staff and customers
Approximately 150 million sq.m. of related-party contracted projects reportedly at a standstill, capping conversion of the pipeline
Gross margins thin and declining (18.3% in FY2025 vs 19.2% in FY2024) under cost inflation and service-quality investment

growth_drivers: Continued expansion of third-party (non-Evergrande) GFA under management, up to 601 million sq.m. at end-2025 (+22.0 million sq.m. YoY)
Push into higher-margin, higher-saturated-revenue non-residential formats: rail transit (+248.6% YoY saturated revenue), hospitals/schools (+54.0% YoY), commercial/industrial parks

Value-added services scale-up: community living services (+10.7% YoY), to-home services (+39.9% YoY), community tourism (new, ~RMB40m revenue, 90,000+ customers), group-buying (+8.5% YoY) and asset management/leasing-sales (+42.1% YoY)

Digital/AI transformation ('Xuanlan' AI quality inspection, 'Yingchuo Service Cloud' platform) aimed at efficiency gains and a new B2B SaaS/technology-licensing revenue stream — nearly 150 external property-service enterprises signed in the technology unit's first year

Potential new-owner catalyst: a successful PAG (or other) acquisition of the 51% controlling stake could remove the Evergrande overhang, improve access to capital/new contracts, and professionalize governance

Balance sheet repair: net current assets turned positive (RMB87.5m) in FY2025 for the first time since 2021, cash and equivalents up ~271% since end-2021 to RMB4.19bn, and zero bank borrowings/gearing

business.description: Continued transmission of risk from related parties has affected conversion of contracted GFA, project profitability, and brand/market expansion; ~150 million sq.m. of related-party contracted projects reportedly at a standstill.

Trade receivables of RMB2,650.8m (FY2025) with a lengthening recovery cycle and unsatisfactory aging; owners' willingness to pay has been damaged by related-party wealth-management product defaults and non-performance of fee commitments made during Evergrande property promotions.

The winding-up of the controlling shareholder (China Evergrande Group) may itself trigger a change of control of the Company and could affect management team stability, as explicitly flagged in the FY2025 annual report's risk factors.
Brand damage from the Evergrande name constrains new contract wins and market expansion even as the company diversifies its client base.

financial.description: RMB13.4 billion of the Group's pledged deposits were seized in 2021-2022 to guarantee China Evergrande Group's debts (fully impaired/provided for in 2021). The company has obtained several favorable, partially effective court judgments against China Evergrande Group and responsible parties for recovery, but management states there remains material uncertainty as to how much (if any) will actually be recovered given Evergrande's liquidation status.
Gross margin fell to 18.3% in FY2025 from 19.2% in FY2024 amid rising service-quality investment and input costs; basic property management margin similarly declined.

The company ran net current liabilities from FY2021 through H1 2025 (e.g., ~RMB518m net current liabilities at June 2025) and relied on creditor agreements and cost controls to fund operations before turning net-current-asset positive at FY2025 year-end.

regulatory.description: Fees charged by property managers in China are strictly monitored by local regulators, constraining pricing power and tying growth to contracted/chargeable GFA rather than fee increases.

regulatory.risk: Employee investigations tied to related-party wealth products
regulatory.description: Some Company subsidiaries/employees were involved in the past promotion and sale of related-party wealth management products to property owners; employees have assisted authorities in investigations into overdue products, creating reputational and potential legal exposure.

macro.description: Broader distress among Chinese developers (upstream market adjustments) pressures new-contract pipeline and owners' ability/willingness to pay fees, even for a company now largely decoupled from direct developer-parent dependency.

macro.risk: No major direct FX risk, but RMB convertibility/repatriation risk for HKEX investors
macro.description: Nearly all revenue, cost and cash is RMB-denominated and PRC-based; the company itself says it faces no material direct FX exposure, but HKEX-domiciled investors are exposed to RMB/HKD cross-currency and capital-control considerations.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Chinese property management industry is in a structural transition from scale-driven expansion to 'lean operation' and from pure maintenance toward a 'property service + lifestyle services' model, per management's own characterization; short-term pressure from a depressed upstream real estate market but considered structurally resilient given recurring, non-discretionary management fee demand.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical — tied to new residential completions/handovers for GFA growth, but the recurring management-fee base provides some defensiveness versus the sharply cyclical property development sector itself.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (zero bank borrowings, nil gearing as of FY2025), though higher rates affect owners' and related parties' ability to pay fees and the broader property sector's health.
key_input_costs: Staff costs (~RMB6.72bn in FY2025, the dominant cost line)

recent_developments.event: China Evergrande Group (3333.HK) delisted from HKEX on 25 August 2025 after failing to meet resumption conditions following its January 2024 court-ordered liquidation.

Evergrande's liquidators hired UBS and CITIC Securities to find buyers for the 51.016% controlling stake in Evergrande Property Services (6666.HK), described by liquidators as a top-priority asset for creditor recovery (unit valued at roughly HK$9-13bn / US$1.1-1.6bn).

Liquidators entered exclusivity talks with Guangdong Provincial Tourism Holdings (Guangdong Tourism Control Group) over the controlling stake; the talks broke down over due-diligence/pricing gaps and were terminated around 25 June 2026.

FY2025 annual report published 27 March 2026 (filed 23 April 2026): revenue RMB13,677.6m (+7.2% YoY), gross profit RMB2,504.6m (+2.5%), net profit RMB1,009.1m (-2.2%), net current assets turned positive (RMB87.5m) for the first time since 2021, and the company recovered ~RMB24.0m in advanced acceptance fees via successful litigation tied to the Deposit Pledge Incident.

Liquidators entered a new exclusivity agreement (announced ~30 September 2026) with Asia-focused investment firm PAG over the controlling 51.016% stake; exclusivity period running 30 business days, set to expire around 27 October 2026. No outcome confirmed as of this report's date.

H1 2026 interim results: revenue ~RMB6,942.7m (+4.5% YoY), gross profit ~RMB1,331.9m (+11% YoY), profit attributable to owners ~RMB517m (vs RMB472m H1 2025), though finance costs nearly doubled to ~RMB79.6m.

guidance.as_of: FY2025 Annual Report (27 March 2026) and H1 2026 interim results (31 August 2026)

items.notes: Management does not issue quantitative forward revenue, margin or EPS guidance; the Chairman's Statement and MD&A provide qualitative strategic priorities only (service quality, third-party expansion, digital/AI transformation, lean cost management).

items.target: Qualitative: deepen 'property service + lifestyle services' model, expand non-residential/high-value formats, accelerate digital/AI transformation, continue cost discipline
items.notes: No specific GFA, margin or profit targets disclosed in the Outlook section of the FY2025 annual report.

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Duan Shengli's statement frames 2025 as a year of having 'successfully resolved risks' with cash flow 'increasingly robust' and operating conditions 'continu[ing] to improve,' citing the swing to positive net current assets and a 271% increase in cash since end-2021. The 2026 outlook emphasizes 'sound operation as the foundation' and incremental, qualitative initiatives rather than numerical targets, reflecting continued uncertainty tied to the pending change-of-control transaction and unresolved related-party recoveries.

bull_case: Balance sheet has visibly stabilized: net current assets turned positive for the first time since 2021, cash more than tripled since end-2021 to ~RMB4.19bn, and the company carries zero bank debt

Business is increasingly decoupled from the former parent — 99.8% of FY2025 revenue now from third parties, with strong third-party new-contract signings (45m sq.m., 92.1% entry rate) and fast growth in higher-margin value-added services

A successful sale of the 51% controlling stake (PAG talks ongoing, exclusivity through ~27 October 2026) could resolve the governance overhang, bring in a credible institutional owner, and potentially unlock capital/new-business opportunities

Favorable court judgments obtained against China Evergrande Group and related parties for recovery of the RMB13.4bn Deposit Pledge Incident losses represent a call option on capital recovery, even though already fully provisioned and with uncertain collectability

Large, diversified scale (601m sq.m. GFA, ~100,500 employees) and growing exposure to resilient institutional/public-service formats (hospitals, schools, rail transit) provide a base of recurring revenue independent of residential developer health
bear_case: Pending change-of-control sale process has already failed once (Guangdong Tourism talks collapsed in June 2026) and the current PAG exclusivity could likewise fail to close, prolonging uncertainty and overhang on the stock

Receivables quality remains weak — trade receivables of RMB2.65bn with a lengthening collection cycle, and owners' willingness to pay has been structurally damaged by the Evergrande wealth-management-product scandal

RMB13.4bn in seized deposits is already fully impaired, and management itself states there is 'material uncertainty' whether any of it will ever be recovered from a liquidated parent with far more creditor claims (~US$45bn) than realizable assets
~150 million sq.m. of related-party contracted GFA remains stalled, representing a meaningful unconverted pipeline that may never materialize into revenue

Gross margins are thin (18.3%) and declining, in a sector facing continued 'upstream market adjustment' pressure from the broader Chinese property downturn, limiting the company's ability to reprice or improve profitability organically
